title: Fix 'command not found' in the macOS Terminal and install the missing tool
summary: The Terminal prints 'command not found' when zsh cannot find a program with the name you typed. The cause is usually a typo, a tool that is not installed, or a folder missing from the search path; these steps check each one and install the tool with Homebrew.

terminal says command not found macos
how to install missing command on mac
терминал мак пишет command not found

prerequisites: Internet connection for the Homebrew search and install steps

steps.explain: Read the message. 'zsh:1: command not found: NAME' means zsh looked for a program called NAME and found none. Check the spelling first, then follow the steps below.
Check whether a program with exactly this name is installed. command -v prints its path, or nothing if it is not found.

placeholders.name: TOOL_NAME
placeholders.description: the name from the error message, without any spaces

steps.expect: A path such as /opt/homebrew/bin/wget means the program is installed. No output means no program with this name is found.

steps.explain: Show the folders zsh searches for programs. A program installed in a folder that is missing from this list is not found.
steps.expect: A list of folders separated by colons, such as /usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin. On Apple Silicon Macs /opt/homebrew/bin should be in the list if Homebrew is installed.

steps.explain: Search the built-in manuals for a word that describes the task, to learn the exact name of the program you need.

placeholders.name: KEYWORD
placeholders.description: a word about the task you want to do

steps.expect: Lines that start with a program name followed by a short description. No lines means the word matched no manual page.

steps.explain: Search Homebrew, the package manager for command-line tools on macOS, for the name. This needs an Internet connection. If brew is not found, Homebrew is not installed.

placeholders.name: TOOL_NAME
placeholders.description: the program name to look for

steps.expect: Matching package names, usually listed under a heading such as ==> Formulae. Nothing listed means the name is not in Homebrew under that name.

steps.explain: Install the tool with Homebrew. Use the exact package name from the search results.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE_NAME
placeholders.description: package name from the brew search results

steps.expect: Homebrew downloads and installs the package, then the prompt returns.

steps.explain: Clear zsh's memory of program locations, so the newly installed tool is found without opening a new Terminal window.

verify.expect: Prints the path of the tool, for example /opt/homebrew/bin/wget. The 'command not found' message no longer appears when you run the tool by name.

source.title: zsh manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
